references.caption: One day, Yashoda was churning curd. Krishna was hungry and he obstructed her from churning and climbed up on her lap to drink milk.
references.observed_reference: Yashoda churns while Krishna climbs onto her lap, matching the stanza opening.
references.mapping_note: One-to-one caption/photo mapping; scene depicts Yashoda churning curd as Krishna climbs into her lap to drink milk.

references.caption:
Yashoda was feeding Krishna with all her love looking at his lotus face and the charming smile. 
Mother Yashodha went away in a haste to quickly hold the milk which had overflown on the fire, leaving Krishna down.
references.observed_reference: A split scene shows feeding and the dairy room, supporting the departure from Krishna to tend the overflowing milk.
references.mapping_note: One-to-one caption/photo mapping; use the first action from the canonical stanza and the caption, and retain the mother leaving to tend the overflowing milk.

references.caption: Krishna dissatisfied with mother leaving him hungry, took the churning rod and broke the butter pot with it in a fit of rage.
references.observed_reference: Krishna sits beside the broken pot and spilled curd with the churning rod, matching the pot-breaking episode.
references.mapping_note: One-to-one caption/photo mapping; Krishna takes the churning rod and breaks the curd pot.

references.caption: Hearing the sound of pot breaking, Yashoda came running from the kitchen. She saw the broken pot and curd spread all over the floor, just like how Krishna's fame spreads in the universe.
references.observed_reference: Yashoda stands over the broken pot and spilled curd, matching her return to the sound.
references.mapping_note: One-to-one caption/photo mapping; Yashoda returns to the broken pot and spilled curd.

references.caption: Sages search and get the vision of the Bhagwan through the path of vedas. Such Bhagwan was not spotted by mother Yashoda. Later she found him standing near the mortar and distributing butter to cat.
references.observed_reference: Krishna eats butter amid monkeys while Yashoda is visible nearby; the canonical stanza’s monkey scene matches the image, though the supplied English caption says cat.
references.mapping_note: Photo 005 depicts monkeys receiving butter while the English caption says cat. Canonical Sanskrit stanza 5 identifies the monkey episode; follow the stanza and show Krishna giving butter to monkeys.

references.caption: Her face quivered with anger, caught hold of Krishna who was having a sweet lotus like face, with fake fear. She looked for rope to tie the mischievous boy to the mortar even while her friends were watching the scene.
references.observed_reference: Yashoda catches the mischievous child and holds a rope, matching the binding attempt.
references.mapping_note: One-to-one caption/photo mapping; Yashoda catches Krishna and reaches for rope to bind him to the mortar.

references.caption: The learned Brahmins and sages seek moksha by attaching themselves with Bhagwan. But here, Yashoda was trying to tie Krishna to the mortar. The rope fell short of two inches everytime she tried to increase the length by attaching some more rope.
references.observed_reference: Yashoda handles the rope beside Krishna, matching the rope-shortfall effort.
references.mapping_note: One-to-one caption/photo mapping; Yashoda adds rope lengths, yet the cord remains two fingers short.

references.caption: While the wonder struck gopikas were watching Yashoda struggling to tie Krishna, she became too tired and exhausted. Krishna,the one who is free from all ties, out of compassion for the mother, allowed her to finally tie him to the mortar.
references.observed_reference: Krishna is tied beside the mortar as the women watch, matching the compassionate consent to be bound.
references.mapping_note: One-to-one caption/photo mapping; exhausted Yashoda sees Krishna permit the binding while gopikas watch.

references.caption: Yashoda told Krishna to remain tied to mortar for long time and went to do her chores. After mother went away, Krishna took the butter, which he had kept in the hole in the mortar before and kept eating it.
references.observed_reference: Image shows Yashoda present with Krishna; caption/stanza describes her having left and Krishna eating butter from the mortar. The actual action and mortar are not visible, so numbering/caption conflicts with scene.
references.mapping_note: Photo 009 mismatch: it shows Yashoda present with Krishna. The canonical stanza and caption say she has left, and Krishna eats butter kept in the mortar hole. Depict that canonical action; do not copy the photo scene.

references.caption:
Only people who have no desires can reach Bhagwan. Still yashoda was able to bind him. Devas and Gods in heaven sung in glory to Bhagwan.
